title: Z
short_synopsis: A magistrate investigates the assassination of a political activist and uncovers a web of state complicity.
long_synopsis: After the killing of a prominent political figure, an investigation reveals the role of powerful institutions in orchestrating and covering up political violence.
political_relevance: The film examines state repression, institutional cover-ups, and the mechanics of authoritarian power.
review_excerpt: A blistering political thriller with procedural intensity and moral urgency.

title: The Lives of Others
short_synopsis: An East German secret police officer becomes deeply involved in the lives of the artists he is assigned to surveil.
long_synopsis: Set in East Berlin, the film explores the moral corrosion of surveillance states and the fragile resistance of intellectual and artistic life under authoritarian rule.
political_relevance: The film is a powerful study of surveillance, censorship, and the human cost of totalitarian bureaucracy.
review_excerpt: Measured, intelligent, and emotionally devastating in its portrait of life under surveillance.

title: Sorry We Missed You
short_synopsis: A working-class family is pushed to the brink by the pressures of precarious gig-economy labor.
long_synopsis: Ken Loach portrays the crushing structural pressures of insecure work, family strain, and economic survival in contemporary Britain.
political_relevance: The film critiques labor precarity, neoliberal working conditions, and the erosion of dignity under modern capitalism.
review_excerpt: A devastating social drama that turns everyday labor into political tragedy.
